name.en: Tokyo Metropolitan Shinjuku East Exit Testing & Counseling Room (Shinjuku Higashiguchi Kensa Sodanshitsu)

address.en: SIL Shinjuku Building 2F, 2-46-3 Kabukicho, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo

location.nearestTransit: Seibu-Shinjuku Station north exit (about 1 min); Shin-Okubo (JR Yamanote, about 5 min); JR Shinjuku east exit (about 10 min)

providers.hours: Mon–Fri 15:00–20:00 (Wednesdays women only); Sat–Sun 13:00–17:00. Closed public holidays (except 1–30 June and 16 Nov–15 Dec) and New Year.

services.note: Free, anonymous HIV test (standard, not rapid) with syphilis tested at the same time; chlamydia and gonorrhoea urine tests only 1–30 June and 16 Nov–15 Dec. Booking required, from 2 weeks ahead: online (Tokyo HIV Testing Booking Site) or the booking centre on 03-6694-3566 (10:00–20:00). Results a week later, in person only; no certificates. Test at least 60 days after a possible exposure for an accurate result. Wednesdays are for women only. The page doesn't mention English support. It doesn't provide PrEP, PEP or treatment (testing site only).

Testing site only (no PrEP, PEP or treatment).

name.en: AIDS Clinical Center (ACC), National Center for Global Health and Medicine Hospital

providers.organization: Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS), formerly NCGM
providers.hours: PEP service: weekdays 08:30–14:00. Appointment centre: weekdays 08:30–17:00.

services.note: Japan's national HIV centre. PEP after sexual exposure (within 72 hours): weekdays 08:30–14:00 at the ACC outpatient clinic; tell reception you want HIV preventive medicine. All self-pay (Japanese insurance doesn't cover PEP): ¥20,000 first consultation plus ¥10,000 per day of medicine (¥280,000 for 28 days) plus tax, ¥10,000 extra outside service hours; credit cards accepted. You get 14 days of ARVs first, then 14 more after blood tests. Outside hours an ER doctor may give one or several days' supply, then you return to ACC. HIV treatment: new patients need a referral letter (patients treated abroad: in Japanese or English) and should bring at least a month's supply of current medicine; HIV drugs are rarely prescribed at the first visit. Interpreter fee ¥7,700/day when needed. Visitors without Japanese insurance contact the International Health Care Center first (+81-3-6228-0749, support@jihs.go.jp; charged ¥30 per point). The hospital's SH clinic for gay and bisexual men wasn't taking new patients in 2026.

providers.hours: Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri 14:30–20:30; Sat 12:00–15:00 and 16:30–20:00. Closed Wed, Sun and public holidays. Last reception 15 min before closing.

services.note: Sexual health clinic with English-speaking doctors, nurses and staff (other languages by phone interpreter). 15-minute HIV test, PrEP and PEP (generics available) and testing/treatment for all STIs. Walk-ins accepted; some services bookable online. Not covered by insurance: you pay in full (cash or card); ¥4,000 to sign overseas insurance forms. name.en: Private Care Clinic Tokyo (Shinjuku)

services.note: Walk-in sexual health clinic with English service. PEP (within 72 hours): ¥77,000 incl. tax for a 30-day set of a generic bictegravir/FTC/TAF tablet, including same-day HIV, hepatitis B and kidney tests and the 1-month test. PrEP: generic, ¥12,100 per month (daily or 30 on-demand pills), ¥5,500 for a 4-pill on-demand set, plus ¥2,750 first consultation; adults 18+. Self-pay only (tests ¥3,850–19,800, treatment ¥3,300–23,100); cash or card. PrEP/PEP reception about 11:00–12:30 and 14:30–19:30. A second branch near Tokyo Station is listed in PLACE TOKYO's PrEP directory.

name.en: TELL Counseling: Psychological Assessment for Children

location.locationNote: Tokyo office in Omotesando; see the contact page for the address.

services.note: English or Japanese assessments for ADHD, autism, developmental and learning problems for under-18s (adults only case by case, usually not accepted); reports always in English. In person at the Tokyo office, intake and feedback online; report about 6 weeks after the last session. Fees (incl. tax): intake ¥24,200–36,300; comprehensive neuropsychological assessment ¥435,600. Parents/guardians start the process. TELL doesn't say it prescribes; its listed psychiatrist wasn't taking appointments, so medication needs a separate doctor. Waitlists may apply.

name.en: Tokyo Mental Health

location.locationNote: Shintomi Therapy Office; psychiatry clinic held at American Clinic Tokyo (3F No.1 Niikura Bldg., 1-7-4 Akasaka, Minato-ku).

services.note: English-language counselling, psychology and psychiatry. Psychological testing for adults and children covers ADHD, learning difficulties and autism (not accepting enquiries for children under 8). Psychiatry by a UK-licensed English-speaking psychiatrist focused on medication for conditions such as depression and anxiety; whether ADHD medication is prescribed isn't stated. Waiting list possible. TRICARE provider.

name.en: Tokyo Metropolitan Children's Medical Center: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry

services.note: Large child and adolescent psychiatry department (202 beds, 14 full-time doctors); developmental disorders such as autism and ADHD are a core focus, with outpatient day care and team care. Book on 042-312-8200. Referral rules, waiting times and medication aren't described; call to ask. English pages available.

name.en: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry (NCNP) Hospital: Child Psychiatry

providers.organization: National Center of Neurology and Psychiatry
providers.hours: Main line weekdays 08:30–17:15; closed weekends, holidays and 29 Dec–3 Jan.

services.note: National psychiatric centre; its child psychiatry department treats neurodevelopmental disorders including autism spectrum disorder and ADHD. First visits are requested online or via the consultation desk; revisits via the booking centre (042-346-2190, weekdays 09:00–15:00). Referral rules and medication aren't described on the pages read.

name.en: National Center for Child Health and Development (NCCHD): Department of Psychosocial Medicine

providers.organization: National Center for Child Health and Development

services.note: Psychiatric and psychological care for children, adolescents and pregnant women, including comprehensive treatment for neurodevelopmental disorders such as ASD and ADHD with medication, psychotherapy and parent support. Reservations 03-5494-7300 (weekdays 09:00–17:00). Patients living overseas must go through a medical coordinator with a referral letter and are charged double the Japanese insurance fee.

name.en: The University of Tokyo Hospital: Department of Child Psychiatry

services.note: Treats ADHD (including with other conditions), autism, tics, learning disabilities and other childhood conditions, with parent training for parents of children with ADHD; inpatient developmental assessment for adults is mentioned under autism. Referral, waiting times and medication aren't described.

name.en: The University of Tokyo Hospital: Neuropsychiatry

services.note: University psychiatry department listing developmental disorders such as autism spectrum disorder and ADHD among its specialties; outpatient care by advance appointment. The page doesn't specify ages, referral or medication; Japanese university hospitals usually expect a referral letter.

name.en: Comprehensive Diabetes Care Center, National Center for Global Health and Medicine Hospital

providers.organization: Japan Institute for Health Security (JIHS), formerly NCGM

services.note: Type 1, type 2, secondary and hereditary diabetes: insulin pumps, CGM and carb counting, education admissions, injection and self-monitoring training, nutrition advice, and a foot care and shoe clinic. Referral letter (dated within about 3 months) and appointment normally required; without one, ¥11,000 may be charged. New patients weekdays 09:00–11:00; urgent cases may be seen outside these times. Visitors without Japanese insurance should contact the International Health Care Center first (+81-3-6228-0749; ¥30 per point).

sources.title: Outpatient consultation for patients without Japanese health insurance
sources.publisher: JIHS Center Hospital, International Health Care Center

name.en: St. Luke's International Hospital: Endocrinology

services.note: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes, mostly as outpatients (insulin can be started in clinic), with Joslin-style education classes; service in Japanese and English. Appointment system: bring a referral letter before calling 03-5550-7120; scheduling can take over a month. The ER is open 24/7 for urgent problems. Uninsured patients pay in full on the day; extra ¥33,000 for same-day/unbooked visits and ¥77,000 out of hours.

name.en: Tokyo Women's Medical University Hospital: Diabetes & Metabolism

services.note: Type 1, type 2, gestational and other diabetes and complications; dedicated clinics for children and young people with type 1 ('Young' sessions), pregnancy, kidney disease and genetic diabetes. Insulin pumps (CSII, SAP, hybrid closed loop; 167 users in 2023) and CGM (FreeStyle Libre 2 and Dexcom G7 available as self-pay options). Team education by nurses, dietitians and pharmacists. Bring a referral letter (referral reception weekdays 07:30–14:00); web first-visit booking available.

name.en: The University of Tokyo Hospital: Diabetes and Metabolic Diseases

services.note: Specialist diabetes outpatients every day; insulin pumps (CSII and sensor-augmented pump), CGM, genetic diagnosis (e.g. MODY), weekly outpatient classes and inpatient education by certified diabetes educators, and a diabetic foot clinic. Children: the hospital's Pediatrics department lists diabetes and endocrine disease. Contact International Patients about visits without Japanese insurance.

name.en: Juntendo University Hospital: Diabetes & Endocrinology

services.note: Diabetes, other lifestyle diseases and hormone disorders, run by certified diabetes and endocrinology specialists. First visits weekdays 08:00–11:00 and Saturdays 08:00–11:00 (not the 2nd Saturday). The hospital's International Health Care Center (03-5802-1985; Japanese, English, Chinese) arranges care for foreign residents and overseas patients; tourists aren't mentioned, so ask.

name.en: Tokyo Metropolitan Children's Medical Center: Endocrinology and Metabolism

services.note: Paediatric endocrinology department; diabetes is among the common conditions treated. A referral letter isn't required. Book on 042-312-8200. The hospital also provides paediatric emergency and critical care.

name.en: National Center for Child Health and Development (NCCHD): Division of Endocrinology and Metabolism

providers.organization: National Center for Child Health and Development

services.note: Type 1 and type 2 diabetes from fetal life to young adulthood, with specialist nurses, dietitians and pharmacists and health and lifestyle education; accepts patients from overseas. Reservations 03-5494-7300 (weekdays 09:00–17:00). Patients living overseas go through a medical coordinator with a referral letter and pay double the Japanese insurance fee.

name.en: Tokyo Medical and Surgical Clinic

providers.hours: Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30; Sat 08:30–13:00. Out-of-hours urgent consultations available.

services.note: International clinic for the foreign community with doctors trained in the US, UK, Australia and New Zealand. Primary care doctors manage chronic conditions including diabetes; same-day appointments for acute problems where possible and out-of-hours urgent consultations; dietitian and podiatry also offered. Not part of Japanese National Health Insurance (self-pay). Book online or by phone.
